  <desc id="process-views-desc">Prepared projection of the approved overview, planning, and implementation process diagrams. Not a SysML semantic model. Overview: Five sequential stages across the software development lifecycle: 01 Work Intake, 02 Lifecycle Planning, 03 Owner Authorization Gate, 04 Lifecycle Implementation, and 05 Completed Result and Evidence. A feedback loop returns requested changes from Owner Authorization back to Planning, an aggregate repair loop operates within in-wave implementation, and a correction path returns findings from Lifecycle-completion system validation to the responsible Implementer. Deployment and release remain under separate authority. Planning: Four sequential planning stages mapping plain SDLC activities to Bearing Delivery Lifecycle roles: 01 Intake and Context (Intake, Architectural Alignment, Scope Definition), 02 Architecture and Integration (Planning and Design, Requirements Engineer when applicable, Systems Modeler, Integration Engineer planning), 03 V&V and Synthesis (Planning Test Engineer, Plan Integrator), and 04 Owner Authorization Gate. An iterative triad between Systems Modeler, Integration Engineer planning, and Planning Test Engineer indicates that linear ordering is unsettled. A feedback loop returns requested changes back to the responsible planning role. Implementation: Implementation lifecycle showing two distinct operational zones: Zone A comprises the repeating declared work-unit loop (01 Baseline Input, 02 Work-Unit Realization with distinct Test Implementer, Product Implementer, and Light Implementer roles, 03 In-Wave V&V and Defect Review with ATE and Reviewer, plus an in-wave repair loop). Zone B comprises the distinct Lifecycle-completion gate (04 Lifecycle-Completion System Validation by Integration Engineer execution running once at Lifecycle completion by default, with a correction path back to Implementers) and 05 Closeout and Evidence Handover. Production release remains under separate authority.</desc>
